# Implement and qualify the v0.1.7 decoupled core, then review its architecture

> **Status:** Proposal; target LayerFS v0.1.7; not a released contract.

## Current owner direction — 2026-09-20

Stages 0–6 are closed at their recorded scope and qualifications. Stage 6's closure is [recorded here](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/issues/171#issuecomment-5737253487); its comparative performance claim was withdrawn under D1, not proven.

**#172 now reviews cluster 1 (content) + cluster 2 (storage).** It replaces the former Stage 7 runtime implementation assignment. Architecture flexibility, pluggability and independent evolution are its top priority. The concrete scenario is integration developing against the public contracts while a separate worktree optimizes C1/C2, followed by adoption of compatible revisions without rewriting integration logic. The review requires a source-backed boundary audit and a reproducible substitution matrix for C1, C2 and their composition.

Integration design follows through co-design pairs #179 (projection/runtime), #180 (commit/history), and #181 (boundary/trust); their subsequent implementation and integrated acceptance scope is defined after design. No runtime implementation is assigned to #172. Earlier comments and the historical continuation below retain their original context.

<!-- stage34-continuation:start -->
## Historical Stages 3–4 continuation (completed; retained for context)

The implementation at `24ef187d4` is partial. #168 still lacks physical inode-value pooling. #169 retains payload identities but walks/rebuilds mapping structure; stored-node reuse, exact reference-root partitions and finality proof are missing. Matching performance/resource evidence is also missing.

```text
existing foundation -> E: physical pooling -> D: stored-tree edits -> qualification
```

Use the continuation prompt embedded in #168 and #169, also saved locally as `docs/roadmap/0.1/0.1.7/component-decoupling/stages-3-4-continuation-prompt.md`. Separate ownership and proof gates replace the broad execution pass; the original acceptance criteria and seven-child dependency graph remain unchanged. Stage 5/6 do not absorb these missing requirements. Keep this parent and #168/#169 open.

Owner-closed #166/#167 stay closed; their explicit residual inventory stays in #174. Do not claim those residuals passed, or reopen unrelated scope. A residual affecting a new Stage 3–4 measurement must be resolved/accounted for before that new claim.
<!-- stage34-continuation:end -->

## Outcome

Replace the content/storage implementation under `core/` with independently callable and measurable C1 (canonical content) and C2 (CAS/physical storage), then review architecture flexibility, pluggability and independent replacement before the subsequent integration co-design work. The first delivery is complete-file construction -> real bounded CAS save -> close/reopen -> authenticated readback, with C1-only, C2-only and integrated timer reports.

```text
stable input -> C1 -> bounded finalized objects -> C2 -> SQLite
              |                                  |
        independently timed                independently timed
```

Package homes for the first implementation are `core/crates/layerfs-content` and `core/crates/layerfs-storage`; reuse existing `layerfs-telemetry`. C2 uses `src/cas/`, `encoding/`, `pack/`, `sqlite/`. C1 uses `src/object/`, `file/`, later `filesystem/`. No checkpoint records or generic logical-summary/facts abstraction belong in C1/C2.

## Seven implementation children

Stage 0 is bundled with Stage 1 so the eight numbered plan stages map to exactly seven child issues:

- [x] #166 — Stages 0–1: establish core contracts and implement independently timed C1 construction (closed 2026-09-17; two Stage-1 coverage gaps carried in #174)
- [x] #167 — Stage 2: implement real CAS/FULL persistence and independent C1/C2 timers (closed 2026-09-17; one acceptance item, F10 report attribution, is carried in #174)
- [x] #168 — Stage 3: complete bounded delta, compression, pooling and pack policy
- [x] #169 — Stage 4: implement localized file edits, decoded COW boundaries and size transitions
- [x] #170 — Stage 5: implement independent filesystem trees, attributes and reference ordering
- [x] #171 — Stage 6: qualify the complete C1/C2 core for correctness, performance and memory
- [ ] #172 — Stage 7: review cluster 1 + cluster 2 architecture flexibility, pluggability and independent evolution

Dependencies follow this order. Stage 7 reviews the qualified core. Subsequent integration design proceeds through #179/#180/#181, which define their implementation and acceptance work after design.

## First handoff: Stages 0–2

Use `docs/roadmap/0.1/0.1.7/component-decoupling/stages-0-2-handoff.md`. The full text will also be embedded in the Stage 2 issue so it remains available while local documentation awaits publication. It specifies 46 planned production files, per-file/directory recommended LOC, external tests, exact commands and reporting requirements.

New C1/C2 production estimate: 4,241–7,479 lines (C1 1,408–2,479; C2 2,833–5,000). These are nonblank/non-comment production-source estimates, not physical line limits or promised reductions. Tests/docs/manifests/examples/tooling are excluded. Deviations are allowed and must be reported honestly.

## Architecture and acceptance

- [ ] All seven children completed for their declared scope with actual code/check/evidence links.
- [x] Real independently callable C1/C2 operations and bounded handoff/read providers, with no hidden runtime or database requirement in C1-only construction.
- [x] Four C2 tables plus justified location/base indexes; exact profile/schema codes, constraints and compatibility documented before persistence. Implemented at 19 columns / `user_version` 1; `acefc3179` added `store_policy.retained_pack_ceiling` for the publication watermark (20 columns, `user_version` 2, v1 rejected rather than migrated).
- [ ] No generic canonical payload spool; named reference-ordering resources and conditional singleton/index removals have explicit bounds/proofs.
- [ ] Exact canonical identity, CDC/extent behavior, small/large/empty transitions, collision/dependency integrity and successful-version retention preserved across the completed core. Use the closed stage receipts for the proven scope and explicit waivers; Stage 7 separately reviews architectural replaceability.
- [x] Stage 6 qualification completed at its frozen scope; D1 withdrew the comparative claim. Separate retained-history acceptance and historical waivers remain explicit; no source-only speed claim.
- [x] Per-commit production LOC and estimate-versus-actual file/directory reports complete.
- [ ] Stage 7 establishes source-backed flexibility/pluggability verdicts and unchanged-consumer substitution evidence for compatible C1/C2 revisions. Subsequent integration design belongs to #179/#180/#181. Remote/cloud providers remain unsupported until they satisfy the exact contract; Cloudflare DO/D1 conflict with current no-WAL policy.

Do not close this parent when only Stages 0–2 are done. Root reference retirement, release/tag/deployment and full release closure remain separate qualified actions.

## Context and design availability

Release tracking: #155. Design discussion: #160. Standalone timer: completed #161. Diff/conflict/resolution is deferred to #164 (v0.2.0).

Reviewed design directory: `docs/roadmap/0.1/0.1.7/component-decoupling/`. Its implementation plan and later owner rules supersede stale retry/checkpoint/durability wording in older design discussion. Some reviewed files are currently local uncommitted changes; do not assume main already contains them. This issue is self-contained about scope; preserve/carry the reviewed specification into the implementation checkout. Creating this issue is not implementation or performance evidence.

## Non-negotiable rules

- No retry, fallback, fsync/fdatasync/sync_all/sync_data, WAL or added crash-durability system. Preserve runtime SQL atomicity/abort with MEMORY journaling, synchronous OFF and zero busy timeout. Unknown acknowledgement is failure; no resend/poll/destructive guess.
- No third-party patches, forks, vendoring or registry edits. Use existing pins and locked builds.
- Production files <=999 physical lines; lib.rs/mod.rs <=200 and declaration/delegation only. Product src has no tests, mocks, fault injection, test-only cfg or test-only public APIs. External tests use real production bodies.
- Core contains the replacement; root crates remain an isolated reference, never a dependency or fallback. C1/C2 do not depend on Workspace, history, FUSE, daemon or Monitor.
- C1-only construction, C2-only real save/read and integrated timing are required, with honest included/excluded work, bounded detail and unchanged on/off behavior. No per-object trace growth or invented duration arithmetic.
- Every commit reports exact production LOC before/after/signed delta with reference/core/combined subtotals. Include shipped runtime SQL; exclude tests/docs/tools. Report estimated-versus-actual size honestly; never remove validation to hit an estimate.
- Preserve actual batching, localized algorithms, locators, useful bounded caches and supported profile semantics. No warm-cache credit, extra workers, hidden spool or fabricated PASS. No CI or aggregate pre-push gate exists. tools/preflight.sh is permanently retired; run explicit affected-workspace checks individually, never an aggregate replacement.
title: v0.1.7: implement and qualify the decoupled C1/C2 core, then review architecture flexibility
